baseline.authority: AGENTS.md; the append-only retention ledger contract recorded in V17__backup_artefact_manifest.sql (BK-18 / C7 section 3.5)
baseline.decision: Product Owner directive 2026-09-20: an administrator must be able to delete a device. The protection is not a refusal, it is an informed choice -- tell the operator the device still has backups and let them choose to retain them or remove them as well. Silent loss stays prevented by writing the ledger event, not by blocking the delete.
baseline.observed: Deleting a device returns 500. The live stack trace is PSQLException: permission denied for table artefact_retention_ledger, raised from JooqDeviceRepository.deleteDevice. The cascade issues DELETE against artefact_retention_ledger and backup_artefact_retrieval, and the app role holds only SELECT and INSERT on both because V17 and V18 grant exactly that: the ledger is append-only from its first row and the retrieval table is the fail-closed audit of who fetched a backup.

recommended_reasoning.reason: A bounded fix inside an already-frozen evidence contract. The contract states the invariant, so the work is deterministic; the only judgement is the removal shape, and its options are named in risks.

requirements: An administrator can delete any device, including one that has backups
artefact_retention_ledger and backup_artefact_retrieval are never DELETEd from; the application role's grants stay SELECT, INSERT
Removing an artefact appends a 'removed' event to artefact_retention_ledger carrying its retention tier, so a removal is never silent
Retaining artefacts leaves them readable and locatable after the device row is gone
The operator is told the artefact count before the deletion happens, not after
No secret, device hostname, serial or management address is introduced into any log line, error body or UI string this movement adds
risks: artefact_retention_ledger.artefact_id is a foreign key onto backup_artefact(artefact_id), so deleting the artefact row breaks the ledger's reference. Removal therefore cannot be a plain DELETE of the artefact row. Choose one shape and say which in the SESSION_CLOSE: mark the manifest row removed and free the vault bytes, or relax the reference so the ledger outlives the row. Do not silently cascade.
The delete path runs inside auditedTransactionBoundary; ledger writes must join that transaction so a partial delete cannot leave artefacts unrecorded
The vault bytes live outside the database; freeing them is not transactional with it, so decide and state the order of operations
